command: pnpm --filter cotal-ai... build && pnpm smoke:delivery-broker-coupling && pnpm smoke:delivery-lease:auth

mutations.name: the daemon never reacts to a lease watch event (the loss window reverts to the renew period)
mutations.expectRed: L4 and the daemon's log names the watch-driven loss rather than a renew failure
mutations.cell: L4 and the daemon's log names the watch-driven loss rather than a renew failure
mutations.note: The watch trigger's own-write/foreign-write branch removed: every event, including the daemon's own acquire/renew/ready writes, is ignored. The loser still exits via the renew tick, so L5 can stay green while the loss window is back to ~15s; the cells that die are L3 (the 5s bound) and L4 (the watch-named loss line). Measured at the base shape: 14588ms.

mutations.name: the registry resolution is dropped (a registered space is dialed at the bare loopback default again)
mutations.expectRed: R1 the subject daemon dialed the RECORDED broker (banner), no --server given
mutations.cell: R1 the subject daemon dialed the RECORDED broker (banner), no --server given
mutations.note: The assignment of the recorded server to the dial target removed, so `server` keeps `v.server ?? DEFAULT_SERVER` for a registered space and the daemon dials the loopback default instead of the suite's broker. The banner then reads `no meshes entry ... the local default`, so R1 dies on the dial-target assertion; R2 also dies (its refusal names 127.0.0.1:4222 rather than the recorded dead port), but R1 is the cell named here: it is the registry-resolved dial itself, not a downstream refusal.

mutations.name: the --server-vs-record mismatch refusal is dropped (a differing --server silently overrides the record)
mutations.expectRed: R3 an explicit --server differing from the record is refused before any dial, naming both URLs
mutations.cell: R3 an explicit --server differing from the record is refused before any dial, naming both URLs
mutations.note: The refusal removed: `server` stays the explicit `--server`, R3's daemon dials the suite's live broker and comes up instead of exiting with the both-URLs message, so the `done()` wait times out and the cell's log holds a `✓ delivery daemon up` line instead of the refusal. R2 and R4 still pass: they never pass `--server`.

mutations.name: the root-mismatch refusal is dropped (a record for another workspace root is served against this root's tenant material)
mutations.expectRed: R4 a record for a different workspace root is refused before any dial, naming both roots
mutations.cell: R4 a record for a different workspace root is refused before any dial, naming both roots
mutations.note: The refusal removed: R4's record names the suite's live broker under a different root, so the daemon dials it and comes up rather than exiting with both roots named; the cell times out on `done()` and its log never names the other root. R2 and R3 still pass (R2's record root matches; R3 refuses on --server first).

mutations.name: the permission-denial branch is collapsed back into the conflict sentence (#374's own bug shape)
mutations.expectRed: R6 the denial never says another daemon is running
mutations.cell: R6 the denial never says another daemon is running
mutations.note: The permission-denied branch's own message replaced with the CAS-loss conflict sentence, reproducing #374's original bug: a denial once again reports 'a live lease already exists ... another delivery daemon is running'. R6's other assertions (exit code, unwritten row) still pass since only the printed line changed, so only the two denial-content cells die.

why: THE COMMAND REBUILDS BEFORE EVERY RUN: the daemon child runs `bin/cotal.ts` via tsx, which
resolves workspace packages to their compiled dist, so a source mutant is invisible until
built. The first version of this fixture ran the suites bare and the mutant read UNGRADABLE
for exactly that reason (measured: the suite passed with the trigger removed because the
child never saw it). The `pnpm --filter cotal-ai... build` prefix is what makes the mutation
reach the process under test; the tool's restore verifies source, not dist, so rebuild once
by hand after a proof to keep dist matched to the restored source.
